channel.title: National Circus – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from National Circus – Bias and Credibility (nationalcircus.com)

item.title: When a Ballot 'Discrepancy' Hits, Who Controls the Story, and Who Counts the Paper - National Circus
item.description: A new state-level ballot discrepancy inquiry is spotlighting the gap between political messaging and the unglamorous math of election reconciliation. The stakes are less about one number and more about who gets to declare victory in public before investigators finish the paperwork.

item.title: ICE Agents Sent to Airports as TSA Faces Shutdown Shortages, but What Can They Actually Do? - National Circus
item.description: The Trump administration sent ICE agents to more than a dozen major airports as TSA staffing strains intensified during a shutdown fight. A former acting ICE director says the move adds visibility, not trained screeners, raising questions about optics, authority, and results.

item.title: VOA Journalists Sue, Alleging Trump Appointees Turned Broadcasts Into Talking Points - National Circus
item.description: Four Voice of America journalists filed suit in federal court, saying remaining broadcasts are being shaped to echo White House messaging, while the agency argues taxpayer-funded programming should reflect U.S. policy and national interests.

item.title: Trump Presses Shutdown Deal on Voter ID, Signals Optimism on Iran - National Circus
item.description: In a CBS News segment, Donald Trump urged GOP leaders to hold the line on ending a partial government shutdown unless Democrats backed a voter ID bill, while also projecting confidence about a possible agreement with Iran.

item.title: Mullin Takes DHS, Rand Paul Breaks Ranks, and a Shutdown Clock Ticks - National Circus
item.description: The Senate confirmed Oklahoma Republican Markwayne Mullin to run DHS in a 54-45 vote, handing Trump a reset button as a prolonged funding shutdown and air-travel strains raise the pressure for a deal.

item.title: Trump Calls DOJ Biased, Federal Judges Keep Demanding Ethics Receipts - National Circus
item.description: DOJ ethics rules are written to keep politics out of prosecutions, but in Trump-related fights, federal judges are the ones turning those rules into leverage, deadlines, and, sometimes, case-changing decisions.

item.title: Hegseth vs Kelly, the Iran War Argument Moving from TV to the Senate - National Circus
item.description: A public clash between Fox host Pete Hegseth and Sen. Mark Kelly is resurfacing an old Washington problem: if the U.S. edges toward a direct Iran fight, who actually gets to say yes.

item.title: Trump Wants a White House Ballroom, and Washington Is Already Counting the Conflicts - National Circus
item.description: Donald Trump has revived talk of adding a ballroom to the White House complex, a project that blurs the line between personal branding and public property. The idea raises predictable questions about oversight, fundraising, contractors, and who gets to put their stamp on America's most protected address.

item.title: Minnesota's Title IX Showdown Puts DOJ's Transgender Theory to the Test - National Circus
item.description: A fight over transgender athletes in Minnesota is forcing a blunt question: Does Title IX's ban on sex discrimination cover gender identity in sports, even as federal regulators keep athletics rules unresolved and courts keep splitting.

item.title: Mullin Talks Like a Unifier at DHS, but the Deportation Machine Looks Bigger - National Circus
item.description: Markwayne Mullin arrived at DHS with calmer rhetoric after Kristi Noem's exit, but the administration's mass-removal target, funding streams, and detention-and-deportation infrastructure described in recent reporting point to continuity, not retreat.

item.title: Trump's Podcaster Allies Smell a New Iran War, and Their Patience Is Running Out - National Circus
item.description: A slice of Trump's anti-woke, free-speech-friendly media allies is publicly balking at the idea of a new Iran conflict. The split matters because these voices helped sell an anti-establishment brand, and war talk tests that promise.

item.title: Trump Says Sanctioned Russian Tanker Can Deliver Oil to Cuba - National Circus
item.description: Trump signaled a rare exception to his Cuba pressure campaign, saying he is fine with a sanctioned Russian tanker delivering oil, even as U.S. policy has tightened the island's fuel squeeze and Moscow frames the shipment as humanitarian.

item.title: Spain Shuts Its Skies to U.S. Iran War Flights, Testing NATO's Unwritten Rules - National Circus
item.description: Spain says U.S. planes tied to the Iran war cannot use Spanish airspace, extending Madrid's earlier refusal to allow the use of jointly run bases. The move sharpens a standoff with Washington that already includes trade threats and awkward questions for NATO allies.

item.title: Trump Takes Birthright Citizenship to the Supreme Court, and a 19th-Century Case Looms - National Circus
item.description: The Supreme Court is set to hear Trump v. Barbara, a challenge to President Trump's executive order that would deny citizenship to some U.S.-born children based on their parents' immigration status. The fight centers on the 14th Amendment, a federal statute, and the long shadow of United States v. Wong Kim Ark.

item.title: Trump Talks Peace, While US Forces Stack Up Near Iran - National Circus
item.description: CBS News reports hundreds of US special operations troops have moved into the Middle East alongside thousands of Marines and Army paratroopers, giving President Trump new military options against Iran even as he publicly signals confidence about a deal.
